A1.justification: Both complete, readable 19-page PDFs describe FairJudge. The main text, tables, equations, and appendices can be matched despite reformatting and table renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original FairJudge benchmark evaluations, training-stage ablations, consistency measurements, inference timings, and dataset analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original FairJudge evaluations, ablations, consistency measurements, timings, and appendix dataset analyses.

M1.justification: The judging policy, rubric-conditioned SFT, debiasing DPO, consistency-oriented GRPO, and Full/Fast outputs remain unchanged. Appendix A retains the same objectives, reward function, and Algorithm 1.

E1.justification: Training data and evaluation coverage remain the same: PandaLM, JudgeLM, FairJudge-Benchmark-1K, Reward-Bench, and the multimodal evaluation suite. Figure 9's revised caption describes domains already present in the unchanged chart.

E2.justification: The three benchmark blocks in v1 Table 2 identify Qwen3-VL-8B, whereas v2 Table 1 identifies Qwen3-8B with identical scores. These models are separately listed in Tables 4 and 5, making this a meaningful reported comparator-identity revision; whether it corrects labeling or reflects an actual replacement is unexplained. Other comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The documented benchmark separation, judgment metrics, 2B/4B/8B FairJudge configurations, and timing protocol using 1,000 samples on an RTX 4090 remain unchanged. No revised evaluation procedure is established.

E4.justification: v2 removes appendix Table 7's supplementary comparison of FairJudge_speed and FairJudge_speed_res under different judge settings. Its labels do not clearly define the variants. Training-stage ablations, cross-mode consistency evaluation, case studies, and sampling analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The reward normalization statistics in the GRPO objective are unchanged algorithmic quantities.

E6.justification: All numerical values in the six matched main tables remain unchanged. Removing appendix Table 7 deletes variant results, including the FairJudge_speed_res/pandLM row with values 73.54, 73.13, 59.31, and 60.55. Sections 4.1 and 4.2 also correct the reported scaling trend and ablation ranking to match the retained tables.

T1.justification: The conditional-policy formulation, Equations (1)-(8), DPO and GRPO definitions, and consistency predicate retain the same mathematical content. Appendix reflow and notation rendering introduce no new assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows broad outperformance and debiasing claims to competitive or stronger performance on judge-oriented tasks and reductions in selected biases. The conclusion presents FairJudge as a practical step with boundaries, while retaining the adaptive, debiased, and consistent judging contributions.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 retracts the monotonic scaling interpretation. Section 4.2 replaces GRPO's claimed dominant ablation impact with SFT's foundational role, supported by the largest macro-F1 drops, and acknowledges metric-specific exceptions. The conclusion adds substantive limits concerning rubric/domain/bias coverage, the benchmark's shared construction pipeline, and untested larger backbones.

D1.justification: v2 removes the abstract's commitment to release all resources after acceptance. Both introductions still describe the datasets as publicly released, and neither PDF supplies access links, so actual availability changes cannot be established. Implementation, reward-processing, hardware, and timing details otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited-work set and related-work positioning are retained. Flex-Judge's citation changes from a 2025 preprint to a 2026 proceedings entry with an updated title and the same authors; this is a publication update rather than a new research comparison.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the ablation discussion, qualifies the abstract and conclusion, revises two results-section headings, and corrects grammar and figure references. Affiliations, conflict disclosure, and acknowledgements are updated, while the overall section structure and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: The paper adopts an ICML layout with revised title and author formatting, typography, columns, running headers, and float placement. The main comparison and ablation tables exchange order, Figure 4 moves, Algorithm 1 fits on one page, and Table 7 disappears. Figure 9's incorrect label-distribution caption is replaced with a description of its unchanged domain-cluster chart.

improvement.justification: v2 improves evidential accuracy by correcting the unsupported monotonic-scaling and GRPO-dominance interpretations, fixing Figure 9's caption, and stating concrete evaluation limitations. These gains are tempered by removing the poorly labeled appendix variant results while retaining Section 4.6's marginal-degradation claim, and by leaving the Qwen comparator relabeling unexplained. Overall, the clearer interpretation provides a limited quality improvement.
